message.content:
You are reviewing one step of an AI pipeline in the repo /Users/atahankilic/Documents/ehl-munich-final (BMW hackathon: turn customer feedback + BMW data + cited web research into evidence-linked customer requirements for successor BMW cars; PM in the loop; OpenAI only; $100 total budget, $7.38 spent; cheap model `gpt-6-luna`, reasoning model `gpt-6.1-sol`, embeddings text-embedding-3-small; all calls through the budget-guarded wrapper src/bmw_req/llm/). Read AGENTS.md first (rules: raw data confidential, traceability, evidence vs assumption, customer-facing scope only, markets differ, future needs). READ-ONLY: do not edit files, do not make any paid/API calls, do not read files under "challange information document/".

STEP UNDER REVIEW: **Classify** — turning every raw source into structured signals. We are about to run a FRESH extraction of all 10,128 customer comments, so this is the moment to improve the design.

Read: src/bmw_req/pipeline/extract.py, run_extract.py, recheck.py, study_findings.py, foundation/DECISIONS.md entries D-022, D-023, D-024, D-026, D-038, foundation/documents/validation-report.md, foundation/documents/requirement-model.md, foundation/documents/data-inventory.md, scripts/benchmark_extraction.py and whatever is in data/eval/ (benchmarks), plus the new checkpoint layer src/bmw_req/checkpoints.py (D-041/D-042: two checkpoints cp1 JAN 26 / cp2 JUL 26; `checkpoint_run` + `track` lineage where a cp2 run must build on the cp1 run; source_item.kind includes `research` = 1,028 cited web items in research/checkpoints/checkpoints.json with fields topic/kind/entity/metric/value/yoy/customer_relevance). You may query the local DB read-only: `sqlite3 data/app.db` (tables signal, verbatim_extraction, source_item, study_metric) to measure quality issues (e.g. category distribution, unverified quotes, support_question share, signals per comment, like vs complaint balance, duplicates).

Deliver (≤ 700 words, concrete, cite file:line and numbers you measured):
1. What the current extraction does well and its measurable weaknesses (schema, taxonomy, prompt, batching, cost, quote verification, defect vs requirement handling, multilingual, Source D prompts, etc.).
2. A proposed **extract-v4** design: output schema per signal (fields, enums), taxonomy (customer-facing categories + finer aspect/component), how to capture intensity/severity, need vs feature vs defect, future-oriented wants, market-relevant context; prompt strategy; batch size, model, Flex/caching; expected cost for 10,128 comments.
3. How to classify the OTHER sources into the same signal space: research items (1,028; luna extraction or rules from existing fields?), customer study items (391; rule-based from z-scores/top-2?), options (458) and sales (as context entities, not signals). Give rules and costs.
4. How classify fits the checkpoint lineage (it is per-item and time-independent — say how cp1/cp2 runs should reuse results, what tracks to write).
5. An evaluation plan to SHOW improvement vs extract-v3 with numbers (what to measure, on which sample, cheaply).
End with a prioritized list of changes (must / should / could).

# AGENTS.md

Hackathon project for the **BMW "AI for Product Decision Making"** challenge: an AI app that turns customer feedback, BMW product/sales data and web research into **prioritized, evidence-linked customer requirements** for successor BMW vehicles, with a **product manager (PM) in the loop** and a **full audit trail**.

**Portfolio-level by design:** multiple models, markets, shared platforms (CLAR, FAAR → Neue Klasse) and plants from day one. The 5 Series (G60 + China LWB G68) is the deepest example; F70 and G70 use the same pipeline. **LLM provider: OpenAI.** Stack: Python 3.12/uv, LangGraph, SQLite + sqlite-vec, no graph DB, Streamlit (D-015–D-020).

## Session start — mandatory

Read, in order (short):
1. `foundation/STATE.md` — phase, team, demo path, next steps, budget
2. `foundation/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` — the "Open" section; check for blockers
3. `foundation/DECISIONS.md` — the **Index** table at the top; open full entries only when relevant. Don't re-open settled decisions without new info.

Then read only what your task needs:

| If your task touches… | Read |
|---|---|
| Scope, deliverables, what BMW asked | `documents/challenge-brief.md` |
| BMW data files, counts, quirks | `documents/data-inventory.md` |
| Stack / tooling, budget guard | `documents/tech-stack.md` |
| Workflow, entities, audit rules | `documents/architecture.md` |
| Requirement fields, evidence levels, scoring | `documents/requirement-model.md` |
| Research agents, trust tiers, brand/feasibility checks | `documents/knowledge-base.md` |
| Platforms, plants, BMW sales (cited) | `documents/portfolio-reference.md` (long — search it) |
| Competitors, trends, brand guardrails (cited) | `documents/competitor-landscape.md` (long — search it) |
| BMW Group Report 2025: deliveries, EV share, R&D, NK, digital | `documents/bmw-annual-report-2025.md` |
| Unknown term or code | `documents/glossary.md` |
| Fresh clone / setup | `foundation/README.md` → Fresh clone |

## Session end — mandatory

- Update `foundation/STATE.md` (phase, in progress, next up, one-line session log entry with date).
- Log every decision as `D-xxx` in `foundation/DECISIONS.md`; new questions as `Q-xxx` in `foundation/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`.
- If code changes the stack, schema, or workflow, update the matching doc in `foundation/documents/` in the same change.

## Core rules

1. **Raw data is read-only and confidential.** `challange information document/` (typo is the real folder name) is git-ignored — never modify, move or commit it; never send it anywhere except the agreed LLM provider. Derived data goes to git-ignored `data/`.
2. **Stay in scope.** Customer-facing requirements only (features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment/digital, design & quality perception, driving experience, range/charging as experienced, variants/packages). **Out:** regulatory/homologation, engineering/component specs, pricing/business cases (rough effort as a factor is OK).
3. **Traceability is non-negotiable.** Every finding links to ≥1 source item; every requirement links to ≥1 finding. Keep provenance (file, sheet, row/ID, URL + date for web).
4. **Evidence vs. assumption.** Always separate evidence-backed statements from forward-looking assumptions (3–5 yr horizon); surface conflicting evidence instead of hiding it.
5. **The PM decides, never the AI.** AI only creates/edits in `proposed` status; `approved`/`rejected`/`deferred` require a human actor + rationale. Exception (D-013): AI may recompute *scores* of any requirement (logged); priority/status changes stay proposals.
6. **Audit everything, append-only.** Every change to requirement content, score, priority, evidence or status → an `audit_event` (actor human/ai/system, timestamp, before/after, rationale, model for AI).
7. **Portfolio, not one-offs.** Brands, models, markets, platforms and plants are data/config — never hardcode a derivative or market. Requirements can target several derivative × market combinations.
8. **Brand & segment fit.** Every requirement must fit the brand and the segment (no "cheap efficiency hatch" from BMW, no budget Rolls-Royce). Brand-fit `fail` blocks approval unless a PM overrides with rationale.
9. **Plant & platform feasibility.** A recommendation must be buildable: the derivative's platform and a plant that builds it can serve that market in time (incl. Neue Klasse transition). Used as a feasibility filter only — never output engineering specs. Whether a `fail` blocks approval is open (Q-010: BMW lists "architecture" as out of scope).
10. **Web evidence is cited evidence.** Competitor, sales, demand and expectation facts come from web research with URL, publish/retrieve date and trust tier (T1–T3). LLM opinions are never stored as sources; unverified user claims stay flagged until verified.
11. **Explainable prioritization.** Every score has a visible factor breakdown and plain-language rationale.
12. **OpenAI for all LLM work**; model names via env (`OPENAI_MODEL_*`). Secrets live in `.env` (git-ignored); commit `.env.example` only.
13. **Markets are different customers.** Climate, usage and culture differ — segment findings by market and score/prioritize each derivative × market separately; surface cross-market conflicts (D-011).
14. **Future, not just past.** Derive what customers will need at successor launch (3–5 yr) from predecessor feedback + competitors + trends; tag horizon, Kano class and assumptions (D-012).
15. **Living process, not a one-shot list.** ~2-year process: every prioritization run is snapshotted; AI only *proposes* priority/status changes with their cause; PM decides; history is always visible (D-013).
16. **$100 OpenAI budget, total.** Cheap model (`gpt-6-luna`) for bulk extraction/classification/summaries; `gpt-6.1-sol` only for reasoning-heavy steps; all calls through the budget-guarded wrapper; Flex/Batch + caching; capped web-search calls; pilot before full runs; update the Budget section in `foundation/STATE.md` after paid runs (D-010, thresholds D-014).
17. **Don't decide architecture alone.** The stack is fixed in D-015–D-020; changing it (new framework, store, LangChain, …) needs the team first. The demo data model is open (Q-017).
18. **Hackathon pace.** Ship a working demo path end-to-end before polishing; prefer simple, cached, deterministic pipelines over clever ones. Don't build what's not needed for the demo.

## Quick facts

- Datasets per vehicle: verbatims (xlsx), customer study (xlsx, CN/EU means + US 7-point distribution), sales volumes 2024/25/2030 (xlsx), German option price list (PDF).
- Feedback xlsx has **one row per classification** — dedupe by `ID` when counting verbatims.
- No China verbatims exist; US verbatims dominate G60/G70 (90–95%); F70 has no US data but ~⅓ Japan; almost no EU verbatims for G70. No dates in feedback.
- BMW sales volumes look stylized and conflict with public data (Q-015) — never blend them silently.
- Local anaconda Python is broken for pandas — use a `uv` venv (Python 3.12).

## Commits

Small, descriptive commits; don't commit unless asked. Never commit raw BMW data, `.env`, or local DBs.

      72 src/bmw_req/pipeline/study_findings.py
     253 src/bmw_req/checkpoints.py
      67 scripts/benchmark_extraction.py
     835 total

1	"""Second pass on out-of-scope verdicts with the reasoning model (Q-019, D-023).
     2	
     3	`uv run python -m bmw_req.pipeline.recheck G60 [--workers 4] [--cap-usd 0.3]`
     4	Only verbatims with in_scope = 0 and no recheck yet. A flip to in_scope adds signals (same extractor
     5	version, provenance via signal.llm_usage_id) and writes an audit_event with before/after.
     6	"""
     7	
     8	import argparse
     9	import json
    10	import time
    11	from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
    12	
    13	from bmw_req.db import connect
    14	from bmw_req.llm import LLM, BudgetExceeded, budget
    15	from bmw_req.pipeline.extract import EXTRACTOR_VERSION, INSTRUCTIONS, BatchResult, check_batch, quote_ok
    16	from bmw_req.pipeline.run_extract import insert_signal
    17	
    18	BATCH_SIZE = 25
    19	RECHECK_INSTRUCTIONS = INSTRUCTIONS + """
    20	
    21	SECOND PASS: a first pass judged every verbatim below as out of scope; its reason is given as
    22	first_pass_reason. Re-examine each one. Many verbatims mix dealer, service, sales or charging-network
    23	content with a real product signal — extract every in-scope signal even if most of the verbatim is out of
    24	scope (e.g. "the car only fast charges to 80%, which I hated" is a Range & Charging signal even when a
    25	salesperson is also mentioned; confusion about how a vehicle function works is a difficult_to_use signal).
    26	Keep in_scope=false only if there is truly no customer-facing product signal."""
    27	
    28	
    29	def pending(conn, derivative: str) -> list[dict]:
    30	    rows = conn.execute(
    31	        """SELECT s.id, s.external_id, s.text, s.meta_json, e.out_of_scope_reason
    32	           FROM verbatim_extraction e JOIN source_item s ON s.id = e.source_item_id
    33	           WHERE s.vehicle_model_id = ? AND e.extractor_version = ? AND e.in_scope = 0
    34	             AND e.recheck_llm_usage_id IS NULL
    35	           ORDER BY s.external_id""",
    36	        (derivative, EXTRACTOR_VERSION),
    37	    ).fetchall()
    38	    return [
    39	        {"source_item_id": r["id"], "id": r["external_id"], "text": r["text"] or "",
    40	         "engine": json.loads(r["meta_json"])["engine"], "first_pass_reason": r["out_of_scope_reason"]}
    41	        for r in rows
    42	    ]
    43	
    44	
    45	def recheck_batch(llm: LLM, chunk: list[dict], job: str):
    46	    payload = [{"verbatim_id": v["id"], "engine": v["engine"], "first_pass_reason": v["first_pass_reason"],
    47	                "text": v["text"]} for v in chunk]
    48	    res = llm.generate(
    49	        job=job, tier="smart", instructions=RECHECK_INSTRUCTIONS,
    50	        input=json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False), schema=BatchResult,
    51	        reasoning_effort="low", max_output_tokens=12_000, flex=True,
    52	        prompt_cache_options={"mode": "explicit"},
    53	    )
    54	    return res.parsed, res
    55	
    56	
    57	def store(conn, chunk, batch: BatchResult, usage_id: int, model: str) -> dict:
    58	    by_id = {v["id"]: v for v in chunk}
    59	    flipped = signals = unverified = confirmed = 0
    60	    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    61	    try:
    62	        seen = set()
    63	        for r in batch.results:
    64	            v = by_id.get(r.verbatim_id)
    65	            if v is None or r.verbatim_id in seen:
    66	                continue
    67	            seen.add(r.verbatim_id)
    68	            if r.in_scope and r.signals:
    69	                conn.execute(
    70	                    "UPDATE verbatim_extraction SET in_scope = 1, out_of_scope_reason = NULL, recheck_llm_usage_id = ?"
    71	                    " WHERE source_item_id = ? AND extractor_version = ?",
    72	                    (usage_id, v["source_item_id"], EXTRACTOR_VERSION),
    73	                )
    74	                for s in r.signals:
    75	                    ok = quote_ok(s.quote, v["text"])
    76	                    unverified += not ok
    77	                    insert_signal(conn, v["source_item_id"], s, ok, usage_id)
    78	                    signals += 1
    79	                conn.execute(
    80	                    """INSERT INTO audit_event (actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, field,
    81	                                                old_value, new_value, rationale, model, prompt_ref)
    82	                       VALUES ('ai', 'pipeline.recheck', 'recheck_scope', 'verbatim_extraction', ?, 'in_scope',
    83	                               ?, ?, 'Q-019 second pass on out-of-scope verdict', ?, ?)""",
    84	                    (f"{v['id']}:{EXTRACTOR_VERSION}", json.dumps({"in_scope": 0, "reason": v["first_pass_reason"]}),
    85	                     json.dumps({"in_scope": 1, "signals": len(r.signals)}), model, f"{EXTRACTOR_VERSION}+recheck"),
    86	                )
    87	                flipped += 1
    88	            else:
    89	                conn.execute(
    90	                    "UPDATE verbatim_extraction SET recheck_llm_usage_id = ? WHERE source_item_id = ? AND extractor_version = ?",
    91	                    (usage_id, v["source_item_id"], EXTRACTOR_VERSION),
    92	                )
    93	                confirmed += 1
    94	        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    95	    except BaseException:
    96	        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
    97	        raise
    98	    return {"flipped": flipped, "confirmed": confirmed, "signals": signals, "unverified_quotes": unverified}
    99	
   100	
   101	def main():
   102	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
   103	    ap.add_argument("derivative")
   104	    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=4)
   105	    ap.add_argument("--cap-usd", type=float, default=0.3)
   106	    args = ap.parse_args()
   107	    conn = connect()
   108	    todo = pending(conn, args.derivative)
   109	    chunks = [todo[i:i + BATCH_SIZE] for i in range(0, len(todo), BATCH_SIZE)]
   110	    start = budget.committed_usd(conn)
   111	    print(f"{len(todo)} out-of-scope verbatims → {len(chunks)} calls; committed ${start:.4f}", flush=True)
   112	    job = f"recheck:{args.derivative}:{EXTRACTOR_VERSION}"
   113	
   114	    def work(chunk):
   115	        llm = LLM(conn=connect())
   116	        if budget.committed_usd(llm.conn) - start > args.cap_usd:
   117	            raise BudgetExceeded(f"run cap ${args.cap_usd} reached")
   118	        batch, res = recheck_batch(llm, chunk, job)
   119	        checks = check_batch(chunk, batch)
   120	        return {"cost": res.cost_usd, "missing": len(checks["missing_ids"]),
   121	                **store(llm.conn, chunk, batch, res.usage_id, llm.model_for("smart"))}
   122	
   123	    t0, totals = time.time(), {"flipped": 0, "confirmed": 0, "signals": 0, "unverified_quotes": 0, "missing": 0, "failed": 0}
   124	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(args.workers) as pool:
   125	        for n, f in enumerate(as_completed([pool.submit(work, c) for c in chunks]), 1):
   126	            try:
   127	                r = f.result()

    10	
    11	import json

    14	
    15	from bmw_req.db import connect
    16	
    17	MAP = {"Likes": {"like"}, "Defect": {"defect"}, "Difficult to Use": {"difficult_to_use"}, "Wants": {"want"}}
    18	LENIENT = {"Likes": {"like"}, "Defect": {"defect", "complaint"}, "Difficult to Use": {"difficult_to_use", "defect", "complaint"},
    19	           "Wants": {"want", "complaint"}}
    20	
    21	
    22	def main(derivs):
    23	    conn = connect()
    24	    versions = [r[0] for r in conn.execute("SELECT DISTINCT extractor_version FROM verbatim_extraction ORDER BY 1")]
    25	    out = {}
    26	    for d in derivs:
    27	        items = conn.execute("SELECT id, meta_json FROM source_item WHERE kind = 'feedback' AND vehicle_model_id = ?", (d,)).fetchall()
    28	        labels = {r["id"]: {l["feedback_type"] for l in json.loads(r["meta_json"])["bmw_labels"] if l["feedback_type"]} for r in items}
    29	        for v in versions:
    30	            ext = {r["source_item_id"]: r["in_scope"] for r in conn.execute(
    31	                """SELECT e.source_item_id, e.in_scope FROM verbatim_extraction e JOIN source_item s ON s.id = e.source_item_id
    32	                   WHERE s.vehicle_model_id = ? AND e.extractor_version = ?""", (d, v))}
    33	            if len(ext) < 0.9 * len(items):
    34	                continue
    35	            sig = defaultdict(set)
    36	            for r in conn.execute(
    37	                """SELECT g.source_item_id, g.feedback_type FROM signal g JOIN source_item s ON s.id = g.source_item_id
    38	                   WHERE s.vehicle_model_id = ? AND g.extractor_version = ?""", (d, v)):

   122	    return {
   123	        "missing_ids": sorted(set(by_id) - set(returned)),
   124	        "invented_ids": sorted(set(returned) - set(by_id)),
   125	        "duplicate_ids": sorted({i for i in returned if returned.count(i) > 1}),
   126	        "signals": sum(len(r.signals) for r in batch.results),
   127	        "out_of_scope": sum(not r.in_scope for r in batch.results),
   128	        "bad_quotes": bad_quotes,
   129	    }
     1	"""Run signal extraction over ingested verbatims, in parallel Flex calls, storing results (D-022).
     2	
     3	`uv run python -m bmw_req.pipeline.run_extract G60 [--ids-file f] [--workers 16] [--cap-usd 1.0]`
     4	Idempotent: verbatims that already have a row for EXTRACTOR_VERSION are skipped.
     5	"""
     6	
     7	import argparse
     8	import json
     9	import random
    10	import sys
    11	import threading
    12	import time
    13	from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
    14	
    15	import openai
    16	
    17	from bmw_req.db import connect
    18	from bmw_req.llm import LLM, BudgetExceeded, budget
    19	from bmw_req.pipeline.extract import EXTRACTOR_VERSION, check_batch, extract_batch, quote_ok
    20	
    21	BATCH_SIZE = 25
    22	RETRIES = 4
    23	
    24	
    25	def pending(conn, derivative: str, ids: list[str] | None) -> list[dict]:
    26	    rows = conn.execute(
    27	        """SELECT s.id, s.external_id, s.text, s.meta_json FROM source_item s
    28	           WHERE s.kind = 'feedback' AND s.vehicle_model_id = ?
    29	             AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM verbatim_extraction e
    30	                             WHERE e.source_item_id = s.id AND e.extractor_version = ?)
    31	           ORDER BY s.external_id""",
    32	        (derivative, EXTRACTOR_VERSION),
    33	    ).fetchall()
    34	    out = [
    35	        {"source_item_id": r["id"], "id": r["external_id"], "text": r["text"] or "",
    36	         "engine": json.loads(r["meta_json"])["engine"]}
    37	        for r in rows
    38	    ]
    39	    if ids is not None:
    40	        out = [v for v in out if v["id"] in set(ids)]
    41	    return out
    42	
    43	
    44	def store(conn, chunk: list[dict], batch, usage_id: int | None, model: str) -> dict:
    45	    by_id = {v["id"]: v for v in chunk}
    46	    stored = signals = unverified = 0
    47	    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    48	    try:
    49	        seen = set()
    50	        for r in batch.results:
    51	            v = by_id.get(r.verbatim_id)
    52	            if v is None or r.verbatim_id in seen:
    53	                continue   # invented or duplicate ID: ignore; missing ones stay pending
    54	            seen.add(r.verbatim_id)
    55	            conn.execute(
    56	                "INSERT INTO verbatim_extraction (source_item_id, extractor_version, in_scope, out_of_scope_reason,"
    57	                " llm_usage_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
    58	                (v["source_item_id"], EXTRACTOR_VERSION, int(r.in_scope), r.out_of_scope_reason, usage_id),
    59	            )
    60	            for s in r.signals:
    61	                ok = quote_ok(s.quote, v["text"])
    62	                unverified += not ok
    63	                insert_signal(conn, v["source_item_id"], s, ok, usage_id)
    64	                signals += 1
    65	            stored += 1
    66	        conn.execute(
    67	            """INSERT INTO audit_event (actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, new_value, model, prompt_ref)
    68	               VALUES ('ai', 'pipeline.extract', 'extract_signals', 'llm_usage', ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
    69	            (str(usage_id), json.dumps({"verbatims": stored, "signals": signals, "unverified_quotes": unverified}),
    70	             model, EXTRACTOR_VERSION),
    71	        )
    72	        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    73	    except BaseException:
    74	        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
    75	        raise
    76	    return {"stored": stored, "signals": signals, "unverified_quotes": unverified}
    77	
    78	
    79	def insert_signal(conn, source_item_id: int, s, quote_verified: bool, usage_id: int | None) -> None:
    80	    conn.execute(
    81	        "INSERT INTO signal (source_item_id, extractor_version, category, topic, feedback_type, severity,"
    82	        " need_statement, quote, quote_verified, llm_usage_id, support_question)"
    83	        " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
    84	        (source_item_id, EXTRACTOR_VERSION, s.category, s.topic, s.feedback_type, s.severity,
    85	         s.need_statement, s.quote, int(quote_verified), usage_id, int(getattr(s, "support_question", False))),
    86	    )
    87	
    88	
    89	_local = threading.local()
    90	
    91	
    92	def _llm() -> LLM:
    93	    if not hasattr(_local, "llm"):
    94	        _local.llm = LLM(conn=connect())
    95	    return _local.llm
    96	
    97	
    98	def run_committed(conn, job: str, first_id: int) -> float:
    99	    """Committed spend of this run only (its job, rows after the run started) — other jobs running in
   100	    parallel must not trip this run's cap."""
   101	    return conn.execute(
   102	        """SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'reserved' THEN reserved_usd ELSE cost_usd END), 0) FROM llm_usage
   103	           WHERE job = ? AND id > ?""", (job, first_id)).fetchone()[0]
   104	
   105	
   106	def process(chunk: list[dict], job: str, cap_usd: float, first_id: int) -> dict:
   107	    llm = _llm()
   108	    for attempt in range(RETRIES):
   109	        if run_committed(llm.conn, job, first_id) > cap_usd:
   110	            raise BudgetExceeded(f"run cap ${cap_usd} reached")
   111	        try:
   112	            batch, res = extract_batch(llm, chunk, job=job)
   113	            break
   114	        except (openai.RateLimitError, openai.APITimeoutError, openai.InternalServerError, openai.APIConnectionError) as e:
   115	            if attempt == RETRIES - 1:
   116	                return {"error": repr(e)[:300], "ids": [v["id"] for v in chunk]}
   117	            time.sleep(15 * 2 ** attempt + random.random() * 5)
   118	    checks = check_batch(chunk, batch)
   119	    stats = store(llm.conn, chunk, batch, res.usage_id, llm.model_for("fast"))
   120	    return {"cost": res.cost_usd, "checks": checks, **stats}
   121	
   122	
   123	def main():
   124	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
   125	    ap.add_argument("derivative")
   126	    ap.add_argument("--ids-file", help="JSON list of verbatim IDs to restrict to")
   127	    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=16)
   128	    ap.add_argument("--cap-usd", type=float, default=1.0, help="abort when this run's committed spend passes this")
   129	    args = ap.parse_args()
   130	
   131	    conn = connect()
   132	    ids = json.load(open(args.ids_file)) if args.ids_file else None
   133	    todo = pending(conn, args.derivative, ids)
   134	    chunks = [todo[i:i + BATCH_SIZE] for i in range(0, len(todo), BATCH_SIZE)]
   135	    start = budget.committed_usd(conn)
   136	    first_id = conn.execute("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(id), 0) FROM llm_usage").fetchone()[0]
   137	    print(f"{len(todo)} verbatims pending → {len(chunks)} calls, {args.workers} workers; committed ${start:.4f}", flush=True)
   138	    job = f"extract:{args.derivative}:{EXTRACTOR_VERSION}"
   139	
   140	    t0 = time.time()
   141	    totals = {"done": 0, "signals": 0, "unverified": 0, "missing": 0, "invented": 0, "failed": 0}
   142	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(args.workers) as pool:
   143	        futures = [pool.submit(process, c, job, args.cap_usd, first_id) for c in chunks]
   144	        for n, f in enumerate(as_completed(futures), 1):
   145	            try:
   146	                r = f.result()
   147	            except BudgetExceeded as e:
   148	                print(f"ABORT: {e}", flush=True)
   149	                for other in futures:
   150	                    other.cancel()
   151	                break
   152	            except Exception as e:   # e.g. structured-output parse failure; the batch stays pending
   153	                totals["failed"] += 1
   154	                print(f"[{n}/{len(chunks)}] FAILED {e!r:.300}", flush=True)
   155	                continue
   156	            if "error" in r:
   157	                totals["failed"] += 1
   158	                print(f"[{n}/{len(chunks)}] FAILED {r['error']}", flush=True)
   159	                continue
   160	            totals["done"] += r["stored"]
   161	            totals["signals"] += r["signals"]
   162	            totals["unverified"] += r["unverified_quotes"]
   163	            totals["missing"] += len(r["checks"]["missing_ids"])
   164	            totals["invented"] += len(r["checks"]["invented_ids"])
   165	            print(f"[{n}/{len(chunks)}] {time.time() - t0:.0f}s ${r['cost']:.4f} | run ${run_committed(conn, job, first_id):.4f}"
   166	                  f" | {totals}", flush=True)
   167	    print(f"DONE in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s: run spend ${budget.spent_usd(conn) - (start):.4f}, "
   168	          f"total spent ${budget.spent_usd(conn):.4f}, committed ${budget.committed_usd(conn):.4f} | {totals}", flush=True)
   169	    if totals["failed"] or totals["missing"]:
   170	        sys.exit(1)
   171	
   172	
   173	if __name__ == "__main__":
   174	    main()

## D-022 — Extraction v2 and signal storage (applies Q-018)
- Date: 2026-10-10
- Decided by: agent; Atahan said "apply the Q-018 fixes and run full G60"
- Status: accepted
- Context: pilot findings (Q-018); the full run needs its output stored.
- Decision:
  - `extract-v2` prompt: new feedback type `complaint` (works as designed, customer dissatisfied); category definitions (trunk/doors → Exterior, HVAC/noise → Comfort & Space, …); stricter quote instruction.
  - Quotes are checked deterministically (contiguous span, whitespace/case normalized); failures are stored with `quote_verified = 0`, not dropped.
  - `prompt_cache_options={"mode": "explicit"}` on extraction calls: the prefix is below the 1,024-token cache minimum, so implicit cache writes were pure +25% input cost.
  - Derivation prompt: explicit horizon and Kano criteria, `horizon_reason`, `kano_drift`, proposed numeric targets marked as assumptions. Not re-validated yet (no derivation run since).
  - New tables: `verbatim_extraction` (one row per verbatim × extractor version, incl. out-of-scope verdict) and `signal` (one row per extracted signal). Findings will be built from signals; `finding_source` still points at `source_item`, so provenance stays verbatim-level.
  - Runner `bmw_req.pipeline.run_extract`: 25 verbatims per call, parallel Flex calls (16 workers), retry with backoff on rate-limit/timeout/5xx, per-run spend cap (default $1), idempotent per extractor version; one `audit_event` per batch (actor ai, model, prompt_ref = extractor version).
- Alternatives considered: storing signals in `source_item.meta_json` — rejected, not queryable for clustering.
- Consequences: changing the prompt means a new `EXTRACTOR_VERSION`; old results stay for comparison.

## D-023 — Re-check out-of-scope verdicts with sol (Q-019 option a)
- Date: 2026-10-10
- Decided by: Atahan ("run the Q-019 re-check"); implementation by agent
- Status: accepted
- Decision:
  - `bmw_req.pipeline.recheck`: verbatims with `in_scope = 0` are re-examined by sol (low effort, Flex) with the first-pass reason and an instruction to extract in-scope parts of mixed verbatims.
  - A flip updates `verbatim_extraction` (in_scope, `recheck_llm_usage_id`), adds signals under the same extractor version, and writes an `audit_event` with before/after. Confirmed verdicts only get `recheck_llm_usage_id`.
  - New column `signal.llm_usage_id` (call/model that produced each signal), backfilled for existing signals; small column-migration helper in `db.py`.
- Consequences: first-pass and re-check signals are distinguishable via `llm_usage.job`. The re-check used a looser rule than the first pass for "customer asked how X works" verbatims → Q-020.


## D-024 — Extraction v3: one scope rule for all derivatives (resolves Q-020)
- Date: 2026-10-10
- Decided by: agent (Atahan delegated full authority over the challenge on 2026-10-10: "you are the sole competitor")
- Status: accepted
- Context: Q-020. v2 + sol re-check treated support-call questions differently depending on the pass; F70/G70 were not extracted yet, so the cheapest moment to make it consistent was before the full runs (Q-020 option c).
- Decision: `extract-v3` for all 10,128 verbatims: mixed verbatims → extract every in-scope part; support-call questions → `difficult_to_use`, severity low, `support_question = 1`; generic praise or unspecified "issues" → out of scope. Scoring weights support questions ×0.5 (option a). v2 rows stay for comparison; everything downstream uses v3.
- Validation: 50-verbatim check incl. 25 recheck flips; benchmark vs BMW labels (`scripts/benchmark_extraction.py`, aggregates only): G60 macro recall v2 0.707 / v3 0.693, lenient recall unchanged; v3 in-scope 91% vs 96% — the 213 newly excluded verbatims are mostly BMW "overall technology" likes and unclassified rows (generic praise), accepted.
- Cost: ≈ $0.31 for all three derivatives (luna Flex).

## D-025 — Verbatim findings by clustering
- Date: 2026-10-10 · Decided by: agent · Status: accepted
- Decision: signals embedded (`text-embedding-3-small`, `signal_embedding` vec table, rowid = signal.id); agglomerative clustering (cosine, average linkage, distance threshold 0.35) within derivative × polarity (improve vs like) × category; clusters with ≥ 3 distinct verbatims become findings (`finding_signal`, `finding_source` with the best quote per verbatim); luna labels title/summary/type/coherence. Findings span the derivative's markets; `metrics_json.by_wave[w].markets[m]` holds verbatims, share of that market's in-scope base, severity-weighted count, types, channels, engines.
- Threshold sweep on G60 (0.30–0.50): 0.35 → 243 findings, 93% signal coverage, mean centroid cohesion 0.88. Result: G60 243, F70 166, G70 see STATE.
- Consequence: findings are never rebuilt in place once requirements link to them (the CLI refuses).

## D-026 — Study, sales, option-list ingest; study findings
- Date: 2026-10-10 · Decided by: agent · Status: accepted
- Decision: deterministic ingest (`bmw_req.ingest.study/sales/options`); study → `study_metric` with z-score/rank within each model × market column (CN/EU means, US net top2−bottom3); one `finding` per study item (`satisfaction_gap` z ≤ −0.8, `satisfaction_strength` z ≥ 0.8, else `satisfaction_level`) — only notable ones are shown to derivation, all can be linked by the evidence linker. Option lists: luna turns DE price-list pages into 458 equipment items, every source line verified against the page text ($0.02). US/CN equipment = DE is an assumption. F70 China 2024 sales cell is a formula with value 0 (noted).

## D-027 — Simulated ingest waves and wave orchestrator (resolves Q-012)
- Date: 2026-10-10 · Decided by: agent · Status: accepted
- Decision: `source_item.wave`: feedback split 50/50 per derivative × channel × market stratum (seed 2026); wave 1 = first half + 2024 sales + option lists + reference + baseline web; wave 2 = second half + customer study + 2025/2030 sales; wave 3 = "market event" web research (2026 launches). Labelled as a simulation everywhere. `bmw_req.pipeline.graph` (LangGraph): open_wave → derive → link_evidence → fit_checks → prioritize. Clusters are computed on all data; a finding is visible from its first wave with wave-specific metrics (documented leak of cluster structure, not of counts).

## D-028 — Derivation v3, evidence linker, portfolio consolidation
- Date: 2026-10-10 · Decided by: agent · Status: accepted
- Decision: sol (high effort, Flex) per vehicle line gets top-110 pain/want + top-30 strength findings with per-market metrics, notable study findings, web findings, market profiles, brand guardrails, sales and existing requirements; proposes NEW requirements only (incremental). Every cited finding/target validated; drafts without valid evidence dropped. derive-v3 prompt fixes after the dry run: incremental effort scale and evidence-based market targeting (v2 put nearly every requirement on every market and rated most effort L). Wave 1 drafts of all lines are consolidated by sol into portfolio requirements where the same need appears in several lines. After derivation the luna evidence linker attaches study items (relation from z: supports/contradicts/context) and web findings per target market.

## D-038 — Requirements must be product decisions; evidence-poor markets can't top the ranking
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan (PM review of the first queued requirement: "what kind of analysis is this?"), implemented by agent · Status: accepted (amends D-028 derivation/consolidation and D-029 scoring)
- Context: the top of the review queue was REQ-0006 "Reliable digital use without interruptions" — (1) a defect complaint restated as a requirement (nobody decides against working software; that is quality engineering), (2) a merge of three different needs (1 Series phone connectivity, 7 Series rear-entertainment start-up, Chinese rivals' rear entertainment) with per-line metrics measuring different things, (3) scored Must 72 in China with **zero** customer comments vs Should 51 in the US with 40 complaints. Cause of (3): D-029 dropped the missing customer-voice factor (30 %) and renormalized, so the remaining factors carried 100 % and the E2 confidence cut (×0.92) was too small. 7 of 39 requirements had a no-comment market on top. "Basic" needs were Must in one market and Could in another.
- Decision:
  1. **Defects → Quality hand-over.** Pain findings with ≥ 50 % defect signals are flagged `quality_issue` in the derivation context and listed on a new *Quality hand-over* page (with evidence, CSV). derive-v7: "X must work reliably" is not a requirement; every draft must state `product_decision` — something BMW could trade off. Coverage rule now targets the biggest pain findings that are *not* quality issues.
  2. **Strict merging.** Consolidation and backlog dedup group drafts only if one product decision satisfies all of them and the metrics measure the same thing; same theme/category is not enough. The linker links web/study evidence only for the same need, not the same theme (Q-021 option c, prompt part).
  3. **Scoring score-v3.** A market without its own usable comment base borrows the car line's comment rate at ×0.5 (labelled "borrowed") instead of dropping the factor; it is capped at the requirement's best comment-backed market unless it has its own study gap AND competitor pressure (both ≥ 0.5) — the cap is a visible modifier. Confidence E3 0.8 → 0.75, E4 0.65 → 0.5. Kano-basic requirements get one proposed priority in every market (the strongest market's band); per-market scores stay visible.
  4. Demo rebuilt from the `evidence` snapshot with these rules.
- Alternatives: hard-filter defect clusters out of derivation (rejected — mixed themes like voice recognition are real capability questions); cap without exception (rejected — China LWB rear-seat comfort is a genuine market difference backed by study + competitors).
- Consequences: China priorities now rest on China's own study + competitor evidence or stay below evidenced markets; the PM sees "borrowed" and "capped" in the score breakdown and the How-it-works waterfall.

## D-039 — New PM frontend: React + three.js over a FastAPI layer, redesigned around the PM's workflow
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan ("discard this python library and use something more suitable for 3D rendering"; "the pages seem out of workflow … looks like AI slop"; delegated: "be bold"; chose stack, direction "Cockpit", demo-first) · implemented by agent · Status: accepted · Supersedes D-019.
- Context: the Streamlit app had six overlapping "priority per car × market" views, two diverging decision screens, three pipeline explanations, a buried wave control and could not render real 3D. Atahan pinned Fey (web) as the visual inspiration.
- Decision:
  1. **Stack.** `api/` — FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8600, one shared SQLite connection behind a lock, every write through `bmw_req.service` / `pipeline.scoring` with actor (X-Actor) + rationale, ActionError → 409, long AI work (wave, challenge) as background jobs. `web/` — Vite + React 19 + TypeScript, TanStack Query, react-router, react-three-fiber/drei (three.js) for the car stage, motion, cmdk. No CORS, localhost only (AGENTS rule 1). Built frontend is served by the API (`web/dist`).

- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan (PM review of the first queued requirement: "what kind of analysis is this?"), implemented by agent · Status: accepted (amends D-028 derivation/consolidation and D-029 scoring)

Cause of (3): D-029 dropped the missing customer-voice factor (30 %) and renormalized, so the remaining factors carried 100 % and the E2 confidence cut (×0.92) was too small. 7 of 39 requirements had a no-comment market on top. - Decision:
  1. **Defects → Quality hand-over.** Pain findings with ≥ 50 % defect signals are flagged `quality_issue` in the derivation context and listed on a new *Quality hand-over* page (with evidence, CSV). derive-v7: "X must work reliably" is not a requirement; every draft must state `product_decision` — something BMW could trade off. Coverage rule now targets the biggest pain findings that are *not* quality issues.
  2. **Strict merging.** Consolidation and backlog dedup group drafts only if one product decision satisfies all of them and the metrics measure the same thing; same theme/category is not enough. Confidence E3 0.8 → 0.75, E4 0.65 → 0.5. Kano-basic requirements get one proposed priority in every market (the strongest market's band); per-market scores stay visible.
  4. Demo rebuilt from the `evidence` snapshot with these rules.
- Alternatives: hard-filter defect clusters out of derivation (rejected — mixed themes like voice recognition are real capability questions); cap without exception (rejected — China LWB rear-seat comfort is a genuine market difference backed by study + competitors).

   196	        st = _state(p, weight) if key in prev else "new"

   204	                     "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", rows)

   206

   208	def finish_run(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: int, stats: dict) -> None:
   209	    """Complete a run; an earlier completed run of the same stage at the same checkpoint is superseded."""

   242	        conn.execute("COMMIT")
   243	    except BaseException:
   244	        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
   245	        raise

   247	            "acquire": [run_acquire(conn, c.id) for c in CHECKPOINTS]}

# Validation Report — judge + QA pass (2026-10-10)

Scope: the `demo` state (53 requirements, 165 targets, 3 runs) plus a live PM flow on `wave1`. Method: aggregate DB queries, three end-to-end traces, code review, Streamlit AppTest for all 11 pages and the PM actions, browser for opening a wave and the inbox. No raw verbatim text was read. The validation cost $0.06 (challenge $0.049; wave 2 replayed mostly from the LLM cache). The DB was restored afterwards (`pre_validation` = `demo` + 2 view events). Fixes: D-034. Open points: Q-021–Q-023.

## 1. Deliverables checklist

| BMW item | Verdict | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| Concept + working prototype | **Pass** | 11 pages render without exceptions (AppTest). Overview shows which steps the AI does and where human gates are. |
| Ingest + web enrichment | **Pass** | 10,128 verbatims, study 391 items, sales, 458 option items, 219 web items with tier and URL. |
| Signals linked to sources | **Pass** | `signal` → `source_item` (verbatim ID, file#sheet). Findings: 0 without a source (benchmark). |
| Unique ID, description, findings + sources | **Pass** | `requirement.id`, `requirement_finding`, `finding_source`. Every requirement has ≥ 1 supporting finding. |
| Priority / score + rationale | **Pass** | Per-target `score_breakdown_json` (factors, points, gaps, rationale). AI band and PM band are kept separate. |
| Evidence level | **Pass** | E1–E4 per target. The requirement shows the best target level, which can look better than a weak market. |
| Future assumptions & uncertainties | **Partial** | The fields are filled everywhere. But 42/53 requirements are `horizon=today` and only 1 is a delighter. The "future needs" story (D-012) is thin. |
| Decision status | **Pass** | proposed / approved / rejected / deferred / challenged. Only humans set it (0 non-human status/priority events). |
| Workflow: AI vs. human | **Pass** | Overview page. `service.py` is the only write path. A brand fail blocks approval (verified live). |
| Audit: sources → findings → **consolidation** → scoring → decision | **Partial** | Every step has events with actor, time, rationale and model. **Consolidation is only partly traceable:** the pre-merge per-line drafts are not stored; there is only a "[merged across …]" note in the summary. |
| Audit: content / score / priority / evidence / status changes | **Pass** | edit (per field, versioned), rescore (with factor delta), set_priority, link_findings / edit_evidence, set_status. Append-only triggers verified (UPDATE/DELETE abort). |
| Access events | **Partial** | Only requirement views and exports are logged. Backlog, audit trail, findings and the inbox are not. |
| Review / challenge / modify / approve / reject | **Pass** | Verified live. Challenge took 26 s and $0.049; its edits became 3 content proposals. |
| Markets differ (mentor) | **Partial** | Per-target scores, conflicts page, CN honestly marked "no data for customer voice". But see Q-023. |
| Continuous re-prioritization (mentor) | **Pass** | Snapshots per run; priority proposals with a factor-level cause (verified in wave 2). |
| Scope (no regulatory / engineering / pricing) | **Pass** | Keyword scan + manual check: clean. Range, charging and fuel targets are phrased as the customer experiences them. |
| Brand fit | **Pass, but untested in data** | 0 brand fails in 165 targets, so the gate is never shown in the demo (it works: tested with a synthetic fail). 6 comfort warns on 7 Series look too strict for luxury. |

## 2. Traces (all chains complete)

- **REQ-0018 G60×US** (highway assistance): 2 US pain clusters (70 + 58 US verbatims), 1 strength cluster cited as contradicting. Score 53 = Should. Customer voice: 123/3,346 verbatims. Study z −0.42 drives the "gap" while a *contradicting* study strength (z +0.91) is ignored by the score. Fit: pass (feasibility warn). PM confirmed Should (scripted). Audit 886 → 1586 complete.
- **REQ-0005 G68×CN** (natural voice): cited CN web T1/T2 (AI cabin assistants), no CN study item on voice. Score 52 Should, driven by future relevance (21.8 pts) + volume. Gaps "customer voice, satisfaction gap" shown, E3 ×0.8 — honest. It is a portfolio merge of 5 targets with per-line metrics in one field (bundled).
- **REQ-0001 portfolio** (tactile controls, F70 + G60/G68 + G70): 57 links. Scripted approval 3 ms after scoring (visible as scripted). The linker kept adding evidence after approval (Q-021), incl. off-topic web findings.

## 3. Ranked findings

| # | Severity | Finding | Evidence | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | High (fixed) | Rejecting a "new requirement" proposal left the requirement `proposed`, in the backlog and in scoring | `decide_proposal` had no reject branch; the inbox text says "reject to drop it" | D-034 + test |
| 2 | High (fixed, D-035) | ~9 cross-line near-duplicate requirements | consolidation only within one run, derivation saw only its own line | Dedup vs whole backlog → `extend` proposals; demo rebuilt (53 → 39) |
| 3 | Medium (fixed) | The app was served on all interfaces (Network/External URL) with confidential data | `lsof *:8501`, streamlit.log | D-034 `server.address=localhost` |
| 4 | Medium | Customer voice barely separates markets; 1 verbatim reads as "driven by customer voice" | median 0.36 for 0–2 verbatims vs 0.69 for 50+ | Q-023 |
| 5 | Medium | Contradicting evidence never affects score or confidence (text only) | `satisfaction_gap` uses min z; web factors use supports only | Q-023 |
| 6 | Medium | Linker changes evidence of approved requirements directly and over-links tangential web findings | REQ-0001 links in waves 2–3; F907/F909/F925 | Q-021 |
| 7 | Medium | Future orientation thin: 42/53 `today`, 1 delighter | requirement table | Prompt: require ≥ ⅓ `at_successor_launch` with trend citations |
| 8 | Medium (fixed) | Wave ≥ 2 "new evidence" cause was false for 5/25 requirements (REQ-0030/31/44/48/49 cite no new finding) | derivation_json vs `first_wave` | D-034 honest cause |
| 9 | Low (fixed) | A stale open priority proposal stays open when a later run agrees with the PM | `run_prioritization` superseded only when it differed | D-034 + test |
| 10 | Low | Brand gate never triggers in demo data (0 fails) | fit_check counts | Show the gate with a seeded example, or say so in the demo |
| 11 | Low | Consolidation is not in the audit trail (pre-merge drafts lost) | `store()` keeps only the merged draft | Store the drafts in derivation_json + a `consolidate` audit event |
| 12 | Low | "Confirm priorities" writes one rationale to all targets (e.g. "CN raised…" on 9 targets) | live audit | Only write changed targets, or per-target rationale |
| 13 | Low | `requirement.first_run_id` is never set; linker/fit audit events lack `run_id` | NULL in all rows | Pass run_id through the graph |
| 14 | Low | Actor is free text with a default "Atahan (PM)"; a lost input attributed my wave-2 run to Atahan | audit `open_wave 2` | Require an explicit name per session |
| 15 | Demo risk | Wave run / challenge block the UI; a failed derive leaves the wave "open" with no re-run button | `node_open` commits first | Rehearse with cached replays; add retry |
| 16 | Info | Self-judging (sol judges sol); brand guardrails unsigned (D-031); clusters computed on all data | known | Say so in the pitch |
# Requirement Model, Evidence Levels & Prioritization

**Status: v4 — as built** (scoring v1, D-029, resolves Q-004; evidence levels computed per target; feasibility non-blocking D-030). Code: `bmw_req/pipeline/scoring.py`.

## Requirement fields (all required by BMW deliverable + our additions)

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `id` | Global `REQ-0001`, stable forever |
| `targets` | One or more (derivative × market) with realization type: `carry_over`, `platform_wide`, `derivative_specific`, `market_variant`, `package`. **Each target has its own score, priority and fit result** (D-011) |
| `horizon` | `today` (fix/keep) or `at_successor_launch` (projected 3–5 yr need) (D-012) |
| `kano_class` / `kano_drift` | basic / performance / delighter, and expected drift by SOP (e.g. delighter → basic) |
| `title` / `description` | Customer-facing, actionable, solution-neutral where possible |
| `category` | Exterior · Interior · Comfort & Space · Infotainment & Digital · Driving Experience · Powertrain (as experienced) · Range & Charging · Driver Assistance (as experienced, scope Q-016) · Variants & Packages · Design & Quality Perception. Powertrain and Driver Assistance follow BMW's process image (image_2) |
| `target_metric` / `acceptance_criteria` | Measurable where possible |
| `linked_findings` → sources | Every requirement ≥ 1 finding; every finding ≥ 1 source |
| `fit_checks` | brand / segment / market / feasibility per target — pass / warn / fail + rationale |
| `score`, `score_breakdown`, `priority` | Per target; Must / Should / Could from score + PM decision; full history via `score_snapshot` |
| `rationale` | Plain-language explanation of score |
| `evidence_level` | See below |
| `assumptions` / `uncertainties` | Forward-looking (3–5 yr) beliefs and what could make them wrong |
| `conflicting_evidence` | Contradicting sources — shown, not hidden |
| `status` | `proposed` → `in_review` → `approved` / `rejected` / `deferred`; `challenged` loops back to `proposed`. AI may only create in `proposed` and set nothing else; every other transition is human (PM) with rationale (AGENTS rule 5) |

## Evidence levels

| Level | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **E1 Strong** | Multiple independent T1 sources agree (verbatims across sources + study gap and/or sales signal) |
| **E2 Moderate** | One strong T1 source, or T1 + T2 |
| **E3 Weak** | Few verbatims or external-only (T2/T3) |
| **E4 Assumption** | Forward-looking trend/expectation without current customer evidence |

## Gates

- **Brand fit = fail** → the requirement cannot be approved without a PM override + rationale (`service.override_gate`).
- **Feasibility** = realization context only (D-030): checked and shown, never blocking, not scored.
- Fit checks: luna first, every warn/fail re-checked by sol (final verdict). `market` fit feeds a score modifier.

## Evidence level (per target, deterministic)

| Level | Rule (verbatims = distinct verbatims of the target's derivative × market behind supporting findings) |
|---|---|
| E1 | ≥ 20 verbatims from ≥ 2 channels AND (study gap supports it OR a T1/T2 web finding) |
| E2 | ≥ 15 verbatims, OR ≥ 3 verbatims + study/T1–T2 web, OR study + T1–T2 web |
| E3 | any verbatim, study item or web finding |
| E4 | nothing but assumptions |

The requirement-level `evidence_level` = best target level.

## Prioritization (scoring v1, D-029)

`score = 100 × Σ wᵢ·vᵢ / Σ wᵢ (over factors WITH data for this target) × confidence + market-fit modifier + effort modifier`, clipped 0–100.

| Factor (vᵢ ∈ 0–1) | Default weight | How |
|---|---|---|
| Customer voice | 30 | severity-weighted share of the market's in-scope feedback behind the supporting verbatim findings (log-saturating); support questions ×0.5; **no data** if the market has < 30 in-scope verbatims (CN, G70 EU) |
| Satisfaction gap | 15 | linked study items for this model × market: −z/2 (pain) or +z/2 (must-not-lose); **no data** before wave 2 / without a linked item |
| Market volume | 15 | BMW sales file (relative only, Q-015): 0.75 × units / max units + 0.25 × 2030 momentum |
| Competitive pressure | 15 | tier-weighted sources of linked competitor-advantage / review-criticism web findings for the market (4 = saturated) |
| Future relevance | 15 | horizon (today 0.3 / successor 0.6) + Kano drift to basic (+0.2) + trend/expectation findings (+0.1 each, ≤ 0.4) |
| Portfolio leverage | 10 | targets / 4 (+0.2 platform-wide) |
| Confidence | multiplier | E1 1.0 · E2 0.92 · E3 0.8 · E4 0.65 |
| Market fit | modifier | pass +2 · warn −5 · fail −10 |
| Effort | modifier | S 0 · M −3 · L −6 |

- Missing factors are renormalized and listed as **evidence gaps** on screen — a market is not punished for missing data, but its evidence level and confidence stay honest (fixes the CN bias of v3).
- Proposed priority bands: **Must ≥ 60, Should ≥ 45, Could < 45**. The AI proposal is shown next to the PM-confirmed priority.
- Every target shows its factor breakdown, gaps, modifiers and a plain-language rationale; weights are PM-editable and versioned (`weights_version`, audited).

## Continuous re-prioritization (D-013)

- Every prioritization run snapshots score, breakdown, rank and priority per requirement-target.
- Scores may be recomputed automatically (logged); **priority and status changes are only proposed** (`change_proposal`) and need a PM decision.
- Each proposal states its cause: which new evidence, weight change, or market shift moved it, and by how much per factor.
- The PM sees a priority timeline per requirement and a "what changed since last run" view.

| `kano_class` / `kano_drift` | basic / performance / delighter, and expected drift by SOP (e.g. delighter → basic) |
| `title` / `description` | Customer-facing, actionable, solution-neutral where possible |
| `category` | Exterior · Interior · Comfort & Space · Infotainment & Digital · Driving Experience · Powertrain (as experienced) · Range & Charging · Driver Assistance (as experienced, scope Q-016) · Variants & Packages · Design & Quality Perception. Powertrain and Driver Assistance follow BMW's process image (image_2) |
| `target_metric` / `acceptance_criteria` | Measurable where possible |
| `linked_findings` → sources | Every requirement ≥ 1 finding; every finding ≥ 1 source |
| `fit_checks` | brand / segment / market / feasibility per target — pass / warn / fail + rationale |
| `score`, `score_breakdown`, `priority` | Per target; Must / Should / Could from score + PM decision; full history via `score_snapshot` |
| `rationale` | Plain-language explanation of score |
| `evidence_level` | See below |
| `assumptions` / `uncertainties` | Forward-looking (3–5 yr) beliefs and what could make them wrong |
| `conflicting_evidence` | Contradicting sources — shown, not hidden |
| `status` | `proposed` → `in_review` → `approved` / `rejected` / `deferred`; `challenged` loops back to `proposed`. AI may only create in `proposed` and set nothing else; every other transition is human (PM) with rationale (AGENTS rule 5) |

## Evidence levels

| Level | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **E1 Strong** | Multiple independent T1 sources agree (verbatims across sources + study gap and/or sales signal) |
| **E2 Moderate** | One strong T1 source, or T1 + T2 |
| **E3 Weak** | Few verbatims or external-only (T2/T3) |
| **E4 Assumption** | Forward-looking trend/expectation without current customer evidence |

## Gates

- **Brand fit = fail** → the requirement cannot be approved without a PM override + rationale (`service.override_gate`).
- **Feasibility** = realization context only (D-030): checked and shown, never blocking, not scored.
- Fit checks: luna first, every warn/fail re-checked by sol (final verdict). `market` fit feeds a score modifier.

## Evidence level (per target, deterministic)

| Level | Rule (verbatims = distinct verbatims of the target's derivative × market behind supporting findings) |
|---|---|
| E1 | ≥ 20 verbatims from ≥ 2 channels AND (study gap supports it OR a T1/T2 web finding) |
| E2 | ≥ 15 verbatims, OR ≥ 3 verbatims + study/T1–T2 web, OR study + T1–T2 web |
| E3 | any verbatim, study item or web finding |
| E4 | nothing but assumptions |

The requirement-level `evidence_level` = best target level.

## Prioritization (scoring v1, D-029)

`score = 100 × Σ wᵢ·vᵢ / Σ wᵢ (over factors WITH data for this target) × confidence + market-fit modifier + effort modifier`, clipped 0–100.

| Factor (vᵢ ∈ 0–1) | Default weight | How |
|---|---|---|
| Customer voice | 30 | severity-weighted share of the market's in-scope feedback behind the supporting verbatim findings (log-saturating); support questions ×0.5; **no data** if the market has < 30 in-scope verbatims (CN, G70 EU) |
| Satisfaction gap | 15 | linked study items for this model × market: −z/2 (pain) or +z/2 (must-not-lose); **no data** before wave 2 / without a linked item |
| Market volume | 15 | BMW sales file (relative only, Q-015): 0.75 × units / max units + 0.25 × 2030 momentum |
| Competitive pressure | 15 | tier-weighted sources of linked competitor-advantage / review-criticism web findings for the market (4 = saturated) |
| Future relevance | 15 | horizon (today 0.3 / successor 0.6) + Kano drift to basic (+0.2) + trend/expectation findings (+0.1 each, ≤ 0.4) |
| Portfolio leverage | 10 | targets / 4 (+0.2 platform-wide) |
| Confidence | multiplier | E1 1.0 · E2 0.92 · E3 0.8 · E4 0.65 |
| Market fit | modifier | pass +2 · warn −5 · fail −10 |
| Effort | modifier | S 0 · M −3 · L −6 |

- Missing factors are renormalized and listed as **evidence gaps** on screen — a market is not punished for missing data, but its evidence level and confidence stay honest (fixes the CN bias of v3).
- Proposed priority bands: **Must ≥ 60, Should ≥ 45, Could < 45**. The AI proposal is shown next to the PM-confirmed priority.
- Every target shows its factor breakdown, gaps, modifiers and a plain-language rationale; weights are PM-editable and versioned (`weights_version`, audited).

## Continuous re-prioritization (D-013)

- Every prioritization run snapshots score, breakdown, rank and priority per requirement-target.
- Scores may be recomputed automatically (logged); **priority and status changes are only proposed** (`change_proposal`) and need a PM decision.
- Each proposal states its cause: which new evidence, weight change, or market shift moved it, and by how much per factor.
- The PM sees a priority timeline per requirement and a "what changed since last run" view.

content.content:
# Data Inventory

All raw files: `challange information document/BMW-Data/` (read-only, git-ignored). Profiled 2026-10-10; re-verified 2026-10-10 (pandas 3 in a `uv` Python 3.12 env + openpyxl/pdftotext).

**Counting rule:** the feedback files have one row per (verbatim × classification). All verbatim counts below are **unique `ID`s** unless a column says "rows".

## 1. Customer feedback (verbatims) — `{F70,G60,G70}_feedback_hackathon.xlsx`

Sheet `Feedback_Explorer`, 12 columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ID` | Verbatim ID, e.g. `G60-0001`. **Not unique per row** — one row per (verbatim × classification). An ID never spans two sources. |
| `Source` | Anonymized channel `Source A`–`D` (interpretation open, Q-005) |
| `Brand`, `Sales Description` | `[BMW]`, `[BMW 5 Series]` |
| `Country` | ISO-2 (US, GB, JP, KR, …) |
| `Derivate (e-code)` | F70 / G60 / G70 |
| `Engine Type` | `ICE`, `PHEV`, `BEVE` (= BEV; the raw value is `BEVE`) |
| `Feedback Type` | `Likes`, `Difficult to Use`, `Defect`, `Wants`, or empty (unclassified) |
| `Customer Feedback` | Free text, mean ~215–225 chars per verbatim (Source D ~125) |
| `Vfc level2 3 Name` | Combined "Component : Issue" label |
| `Vfc level2 Name` | Component / topic (e.g. `Seats`, `Touch screen, operation`, `Electric Range`) |
| `Vfc level3 Name` | Issue type (e.g. `Not user-friendly`, `Like: function`, `Customer request: function`) |

| File | Rows | Verbatims (unique IDs) | Sources (verbatims) | Countries (verbatims) | Engines (verbatims) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 | 4,076 | 2,128 | A 2,128 | GB 1,293, **JP 672**, SE 71, FR 53, AU 16, FI 8, DK 8, KR 4 | ICE 2,128 |
| G60 | 5,005 | 4,000 | B 2,626, A 854, C 384, D 136 | **US 3,610 (90%)**, KR 205, JP 53, GB 36, SE 28, DK 20, CA 18, … | ICE 2,259, BEV 1,363, PHEV 378 |
| G70 | 4,690 | 4,000 | B 2,853, A 695, C 314, D 138 | **US 3,792 (95%)**, KR 137, JP 40, CA 8, GB 8, … | ICE 2,568, BEV 1,129, PHEV 303 |

European verbatims: F70 ~1,430 (67%), G60 ~110, **G70 ~19**. Row counts overstate Source A, which carries the most multi-label rows: G60 Source A has 1,858 rows but only 854 verbatims.

Quirks:
- **Dedupe by `ID`** when counting verbatims; keep all rows as classification labels.
- **Unclassified verbatims:**
  - Source A: `Feedback Type` empty ⇔ `Vfc level2 = no_class_found`. That is 300 of F70's 2,128 verbatims (14%; 27% of rows).
  - Source D: no BMW classification at all.
  - Source C: ~70 verbatims per file have an empty type *and* an empty topic.
  - → Our own LLM classification is needed; the BMW taxonomy is a hint.
- 120 (F70) / 221 (G60) / 211 (G70) distinct `Vfc level2` values incl. `no_class_found`. Top topics: Drivetrain, Handling/Riding, Body equipment, Exterior design, Seats, Touch screen, Electric Range.
- Observed text patterns per source. These are **observations, not channel identities** (Q-005):
  - **A:** all derivatives, many countries (incl. JP/KR), lower-case normalized text ("the car…", "i really…"), so possibly translated.
  - **B:** US only; most verbatims start "Customer stated / mentioned / reported / commented…" (third-person notes).
  - **C:** US only; ~30–40% start "I had a minor/serious problem with…", others "What is…" / "If there…" (structured survey prompts); mostly Difficult-to-Use/Defect.
  - **D:** US only; short; unclassified. Two prompt templates in G60 (checked 2026-10-10): 34 of 136 end with "That is the one thing could be most improved about the <area> of my vehicle" (improvement answers, e.g. "the head rests are too short"); the rest are mostly "love the…" answers. So D mixes "what do you like" and "what could be most improved" — the earlier note that D is **not** improvement feedback was wrong.
- **No China verbatims** for any derivative. There is **no date column** — no time series possible.

## 2. Customer studies — `F70_G60_G68_G70_customer_studies.xlsx`

### Sheet `CN_EU_2025` (76 content rows; openpyxl reports 84 incl. trailing empty rows)
- Columns: China → `BMW 5 Series G68`, `BMW 7 Series G70`; EU → `BMW 1 Series F70`, `BMW 5 Series G60`, `BMW 7 Series G70`.
- 37 categories, each a label row followed by a `Mean` row. Values are **numeric cells** (format `#,##0.00`), range ~6.5–9.9. Scale unconfirmed (0–10 or 1–10?; Q-006).
- **No sample sizes.**
- Categories: overall satisfaction, exterior/interior styling, interior quality, equipment level, safety, squeaks/rattles, value for money, reliability, visibility, controls/displays, smartphone integration, infotainment features + ease of use, navigation, seating comfort, small-item storage, acceleration, roadholding, efficiency, braking, sportiness, prestige, manoeuvrability, ride quality, front/rear roominess, luggage loading + capacity, ingress/egress, environmental friendliness, HVAC, build quality, quietness, driving position, connected services, interior versatility.

### Sheet `US_2025` (929 content rows; openpyxl reports 934)
- Columns: question, `% of column, sample base`, `BMW 5 Series G60`, `BMW 7 Series G70`.
- 103 questions, each block = `Sample total` + 7-point distribution: I Hate It / A Failure / Unsatisfactory / Satisfactory / Excellent / Delightful / I Love It. Shares 0–1; every block sums to 1.0.
- **`Sample total` = 1 is the share base, not a respondent count → no sample sizes.** No significance testing or n-weighting is possible.
- Granular: exterior (proportions, wheels, door handles, lights, door sound), driving (ride, handling, power), interior (materials, seats per row, roominess, storage, cupholders, cargo), climate, audio, controls intuitiveness, NVH, …
- **No F70 in US.**
- Useful derived metrics: top-2-box (Delightful + I Love It), bottom-3-box, net score. CN/EU means and US distributions are **not directly comparable** (Q-006).

## 3. Sales volumes — `sales_volumes.xlsx`

Sheets `F70`, `G60_G68`, `G70`; columns `market, market_code, volume_2024, volume_2025, volume_2030` (2030 = forecast).

| Derivative | EU 25 | CN 25 | US 25 | RoW 25 | Total 24 → 25 → 2030 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 | 85k | 0 | 0 | 28k | 105k → 113k → 118k |
| G60/G68 | 115k | 75k | 78k | 28k | 278.6k → 296k → 316k |
| G70 | 13k | 10k | 12k | 7k | 34k → 42k → 52k |

- The F70 sheet's China 2024 cell (C3) is a **formula** (`=-D3-C10`) with cached value 0, not a typed number (found at ingest 2026-10-10; stored as 0, formula kept in metadata).
- **No powertrain split**, although `data_and_source.png` says "units by powertrain and region". Engine mix can only be inferred from feedback.
- `G60_G68` is one combined sheet, with no G60/G68 split. CN is presumably the G68 LWB.
- **Values look stylized and conflict with public data** (Q-015):
  - All values except one are round thousands.
  - G60/G68 CN is 68k → 75k (+10%) for 2024 → 2025. Public figures point the other way: 5 Series China (China-built) Jan–Nov 2025 was 107,348 per CPCA via Gasgoo, and BMW+MINI China fell 12.5% in 2025 (`competitor-landscape.md`, `portfolio-reference.md`).
  - F70 EU 85k vs. 1 Series Europe 91,931 (Dataforce; "Europe" definitions differ).
  - Until clarified, treat the file as **BMW-internal relative weights**, and surface the conflict instead of mixing both sources.

## 4. Equipment / option lists — `{F70,G60,G70}_OptionList.PDF`

- German-market price lists, **in German**, text-extractable (`pdftotext -layout` works):

  | File | PDF title | Edition | Pages |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | F70 | "BMW 1er Katalog Juli 2026" | Ausgabe 1, 28.05.2026 | 23 |
  | G60 | "BMW 5er **Limousine** Katalog Juli 2026" | Ausgabe 2, 22.06.2026 | 28 |
  | G70 | "BMW 7er Katalog Juli 2026" | Ausgabe 1, 28.05.2026 | 27 |

  The G60 list covers the sedan incl. i5 — **no Touring (G61)**.
- Sections: Fahrzeugpreise (models, power, consumption, price), Serienausstattung(en) (standard equipment per model), M Sportpaket / Pro, Räder & Reifen, Farbwelt, **Sonderausstattungen (options)**, Technische Werte.
- Matrix tables use `■` = standard; options with price.
- Use: baseline "what the car offers today", package structure, gaps vs. competitors.
- The briefing promises equipment "by trim and **market**", but only DE was provided. For US/CN it's an **assumption** that equipment is comparable.

## 5. Briefing material
- `BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf` (2 pages). **Image-only (no text layer):** `pdftotext` returns nothing, so render it (`pdftoppm`) to read it.
- `mission.md`.
- `data_and_source.png`: dataset purpose table.
- `image_1.png`: "1 billion findings → 1,000 requirements → one car" + example verbatims/themes.
- `image_2.png`: reference process.

## Coverage matrix (what we can say where)

| | EU | US | CN | RoW |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F70 | ~1.4k verbatims (GB-heavy), study, sales | — | — | **~690 verbatims (JP 672)**, sales |
| G60/G68 | ~110 verbatims, study, sales | **~3.6k verbatims, detailed study, sales** | study (G68), sales | ~280 verbatims (KR 205, JP, CA), sales |
| G70 | ~19 verbatims (≈ none), study, sales | **~3.8k verbatims, detailed study, sales** | study, sales | ~190 verbatims (KR 137, JP), sales |

- RoW verbatims (JP/KR/CA/AU) are separate customer groups under D-011 — don't fold them into EU.
- External/web data fills gaps: competitors (Mercedes E/S/A-Class, Audi A6/e-tron, Tesla, NIO, XPeng, Li Auto, BYD…), reviews, trends.

-rw-r--r--@ 1 atahankilic  staff  211656704 Oct 11 04:02 data/app.db
CREATE TABLE signal (                -- AI-extracted customer signal; input to findings (D-022)
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, source_item_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_item(id),
    extractor_version TEXT NOT NULL, category TEXT NOT NULL, topic TEXT, feedback_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    severity TEXT, need_statement TEXT, quote TEXT,
    quote_verified INTEGER NOT NULL, llm_usage_id INTEGER REFERENCES llm_usage(id), support_question INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,   -- quote is a contiguous span of the verbatim (whitespace/case normalized)
    FOREIGN KEY (source_item_id, extractor_version) REFERENCES verbatim_extraction(source_item_id, extractor_version)
);
CREATE INDEX ix_signal_source ON signal(source_item_id);
CREATE TABLE verbatim_extraction (   -- one row per verbatim × extractor version (D-022)
    source_item_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_item(id), extractor_version TEXT NOT NULL,
    in_scope INTEGER NOT NULL, out_of_scope_reason TEXT, llm_usage_id INTEGER REFERENCES llm_usage(id),
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')), recheck_llm_usage_id INTEGER REFERENCES llm_usage(id),
    PRIMARY KEY (source_item_id, extractor_version)
);
CREATE TABLE source_item (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    kind TEXT NOT NULL,           -- feedback | study | sales | option_list | web | reference
    ref TEXT NOT NULL,            -- provenance: e.g. 'G60_feedback_hackathon.xlsx#Feedback_Explorer:G60-0001'
    external_id TEXT,             -- e.g. verbatim ID G60-0001
    trust_tier TEXT,              -- T1..T3
    vehicle_model_id TEXT REFERENCES vehicle_model(id), market_code TEXT REFERENCES market(code),
    country TEXT, platform_id TEXT REFERENCES platform(id),
    url TEXT, published_at TEXT, retrieved_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')),
    text TEXT, quote TEXT, meta_json TEXT,
    ingest_batch_id INTEGER REFERENCES ingest_batch(id), wave INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, checkpoint TEXT,
    UNIQUE (kind, ref)
);
CREATE INDEX ix_source_scope ON source_item(vehicle_model_id, market_code);
CREATE TABLE study_metric (           -- one row per study item × model × market (D-026)
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, source_item_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_item(id),
    vehicle_model_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES vehicle_model(id), market_code TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES market(code),
    item TEXT NOT NULL,           -- category / question text as in the file
    scale TEXT NOT NULL,          -- mean_10 (CN/EU means) | dist_7 (US 7-point distribution)
    mean REAL, top2 REAL, bottom3 REAL, net REAL,
    z_within_column REAL,         -- standardized vs. the other items of the same model × market column
    rank_within_column INTEGER, n_items_in_column INTEGER
);
CREATE TABLE track (           -- one entity's state after one run (track-while-scan)
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    run_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES checkpoint_run(id),
    entity_key TEXT NOT NULL,           -- stable across checkpoints (source ref, cluster key, requirement id)
    state TEXT NOT NULL,                -- new | held | strengthened | weakened | lost
    weight REAL,                        -- the number the state is computed from (count, share, score)
    prev_weight REAL,
    payload_json TEXT,
    UNIQUE (run_id, entity_key)
);
CREATE INDEX track_entity ON track(entity_key);
CREATE TABLE checkpoint_run (  -- one stage executed at one checkpoint, on top of its parent's run
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    checkpoint_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES checkpoint(id),
    stage TEXT NOT NULL,                -- acquire | classify | cluster | contextualize | elicit | ...
    parent_run_id INTEGER REFERENCES checkpoint_run(id),
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running',   -- running | completed | failed | superseded
    actor TEXT NOT NULL,
    started_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')), finished_at TEXT,
    stats_json TEXT
);

input.command:
python3 -c "
import sqlite3,re,collections
c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/app.db?mode=ro',uri=True)
cjk=re.compile(r'[぀-ヿ一-鿿가-힯]')
cnt=collections.Counter()
for country,t in c.execute(\"select country,text from source_item where kind='feedback'\"):
    t=t or ''
    if cjk.search(t): cnt[country]+=1
print('CJK verbatims by country',dict(cnt))
# out of scope reasons: bucket by keywords only
b=collections.Counter()
for (r,) in c.execute(\"select out_of_scope_reason from verbatim_extraction where extractor_version='extract-v3' and in_scope=0\"):
    r=(r or '').lower()
    k='generic' if ('generic' in r or 'no specific' in r or 'unspecified' in r or 'vague' in r) else 'dealer/service' if ('dealer' in r or 'service' in r) else 'pricing' if 'pric' in r else 'charging network' if 'network' in r else 'no content' if ('no usable' in r or 'no content' in r or 'empty' in r) else 'other'
    b[k]+=1
print(b)
"

c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/app.db?mode=ro',uri=True)
q='''select s.id, s.text, json_extract(s.meta_json,'\$.channel') ch from source_item s where kind='feedback' '''
items={i:(t or '',ch) for i,t,ch in c.execute(q)}
sig=collections.defaultdict(list)
for i,t,qq,sq,sev in c.execute(\"select source_item_id,feedback_type,quote,support_question,severity from signal where extractor_version='extract-v3'\"): sig[i].append((t,qq,sev))
imp=[i for i,(t,ch) in items.items() if ch=='Source D' and 'most improved' in t.lower()]
cnt=collections.Counter(x[0] for i in imp for x in sig[i]); print('D improve-template', len(imp), cnt)
tmpl=sum(1 for i in imp for x in sig[i] if 'most improved' in (x[1] or '').lower()); print('quotes containing template phrase', tmpl)
# Source C prompts
cp=[i for i,(t,ch) in items.items() if ch=='Source C' and t.lower().startswith('i had a')]
print('C I-had-a', len(cp), collections.Counter(x[0] for i in cp for x in sig[i]))
# Source B 'customer stated' support
b=[i for i,(t,ch) in items.items() if ch=='Source B' and ('asked' in t.lower()[:60] or 'question' in t.lower()[:80])]
print('B asked/question', len(b), collections.Counter(x[0] for i in b for x in sig[i]).most_common(5))
# signals with like + defect in same verbatim
mix=sum(1 for i in sig if {x[0] for x in sig[i]}>={'like','defect'}); print('verbatims with like+defect',mix)
# quote length very short
print('quotes <15 chars', sum(1 for v in sig.values() for x in v if len(x[1] or '')<15))
"

imp=[i for i,(t,ch) in items.items() if ch=='Source D' and 'most improved' in t.lower()]
cnt=collections.Counter(x[0] for i in imp for x in sig[i]); print('D improve-template', len(imp), cnt)
tmpl=sum(1 for i in imp for x in sig[i] if 'most improved' in (x[1] or '').lower()); print('quotes containing template phrase', tmpl)
# Source C prompts
cp=[i for i,(t,ch) in items.items() if ch=='Source C' and t.lower().startswith('i had a')]
print('C I-had-a', len(cp), collections.Counter(x[0] for i in cp for x in sig[i]))
# Source B 'customer stated' support
b=[i for i,(t,ch) in items.items() if ch=='Source B' and ('asked' in t.lower()[:60] or 'question' in t.lower()[:80])]
print('B asked/question', len(b), collections.Counter(x[0] for i in b for x in sig[i]).most_common(5))
# signals with like + defect in same verbatim
mix=sum(1 for i in sig if {x[0] for x in sig[i]}>={'like','defect'}); print('verbatims with like+defect',mix)
# quote length very short
print('quotes <15 chars', sum(1 for v in sig.values() for x in v if len(x[1] or '')<15))
"
